drivingQuestion: Who is the 'man of leisure' whose conjugal interval is every night?
outcomeNote: Two definitions offered side by side; the stories illustrate the Western view

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּדְרַב, דְּאָמַר רַב: כְּגוֹן רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת, דְּאָכֵיל מִדִּידֵיהּ, וְשָׁתֵי מִדִּידֵיהּ, וְגָנֵי בְּטוּלָּא דְאַפַּדְנֵיהּ, וְלָא חָלֵיף פְּרִיסְתְּקָא דְמַלְכָּא אַבָּבֵיהּ. כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר: כְּגוֹן מְפַנְּקִי דְמַעְרְבָא.
segments.en: «Rather, Abaye said:» The mishna should be explained «in accordance with the opinion of Rav, as Rav said:» This is referring to a man «such as Rabbi Shmuel bar Sheilat, who ate his own» food, «drank his own» drinks, «slept in the shade of his own house, and the king’s tax collector [peristaka] did not pass by his door,» as they did not know that he was a man of means. A man like this, who has a steady income and no worries, is called a man of leisure. «When Ravin came» from Eretz Yisrael «he said: For example, the» wealthy, «pampered» men «in the West,» Eretz Yisrael, are called men of leisure. Due to the time they have available and the richness of their diet, they have the ability to satisfy their wives every night.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה קָאֵי בֵּי בָאנֵי. הֲווֹ סָמְכִי לֵיהּ תְּרֵי עַבְדֵי. אִיפְּחִית בֵּי בָאנֵי מִתּוּתֵיהּ, אִיתְרְמִי לֵיהּ עַמּוּדָא, סְלֵיק וְאַסְּקִינְהוּ. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה קָסָלֵיק בְּדַרְגָּא, הֲווֹ סָמְכִי לֵיהּ רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי. אִיפְּחִתָא דַּרְגָּא תּוּתֵיהּ, סְלֵיק וְאַסְּקִינְהוּ. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּהָכִי, לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמִיסְמְכֵיהּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִם כֵּן מָה אַנִּיחַ לְעֵת זִקְנָה?
segments.en: To illustrate this point, the Gemara relates two incidents demonstrating the health and strength of the inhabitants of Eretz Yisrael: «Rabbi Abbahu was» once «standing in the bathhouse and two slaves were supporting» his walking. «The bathhouse collapsed under him» and was destroyed. «He found a pillar,» stood on it and «got out, and pulled them» both «up» with him. Similarly, «Rabbi Yoḥanan was» once «going up stairs,» and «Rav Ami and Rav Asi were supporting» him. «The stair collapsed under him, but he went up and pulled them» both «up» with him. «The Sages said to him: Since» it is clear that you are «so» strong, «why do you need» people «to support you? He said to them: If so,» if I were to expend all my strength now, «what will I leave for» myself in my «old age?»
